Screenshots and check files are in /tmp/frbench/review-w15-merge/steps/.

J1, W15-01 (two projects, Status pull request on in both):
- Projects A and B on bench/shared. I pressed Start in A's Overview and then in B's.
- B's scaffold wrote nothing into A's fr/docs-scaffold PR #1 (the log says why). A's status PR #3 carries A's mark and its visible text has no UUID.
- After B's session: the fr/status head and docs/status.md are unchanged, there is no comment from B and B opened no docs PR. The log has "status pull request not written: another project's status pull request is open".
- A's Overview lists #1 and #3 (01-j1-a-overview-own-docs-prs.png). B's lists only its own task PR #4 (02-j1-b-overview-none-of-as.png).

- FAIL: B's Docs tab reads "Status docs/status.md missing / not written yet" (03-j1-b-docs-tab.png, j1b-checks.json). Yet home/data/projects/<B>/app-status/docs/status.md exists, and the user guide says B "keeps its own status under Docs".

J2, W15-05 and W15-08 (chain A <- B on bench/chain):
- Both PR bodies end "Opened by Forerunner in the session started 2026-11-09 10:17 UTC." with the ids only in the hidden mark.

Within one poll B's row read "#3 waits for changes left in its task's folder: take them out or redo the task." with the folder path and Copy path, and no Merge (05-j2-overview-folder-wait.png). - The commit stayed on B's branch through more polls (09-j3-overview-commit-wait.png).
- I then pushed it to GitHub, as the sentence says. The next poll rebuilt B and the record moved reviewed_head_sha to 8ef38a9, whose top commit is "My own change". The row went back to Merge under "Reviewed by the critic" (10-j3-overview-after-push.png, review-state.json).

J4 (bench/chain3), the same flow with Merge pressed during the commit wait:
- The press was kept ("queued").
- After the push, Forerunner merged #3 by itself. mine.txt, which the critic never read, is now on main (j4-checks.json FAIL).
- I reproduced this in a composed test appended for the run only, then restored (dependent-branches-merge chainWorld: squash A, commit, poll, push, poll). The test fails: after.reviewed_head_sha equals the new head holding notes.txt, and the record says "#2 waits for you to merge it".

J5 (bench/solo, three tasks), W15-55, W15-63 and W15-04:
- I closed #2 on GitHub. The Tasks label read "Accepted · pull request closed" with "#2 was closed without merging."
- A commit pushed to #3's branch was not noticed at the poll: the row kept Merge. After I pressed Merge, the row and the Tasks label read "#3 changed after the review: look at the new commits, then merge it yourself or redo the task." / "Accepted · changed after the review" (21-23). The card offers only I merged it / Leave it open.

- A session then ran the task from main: no rebase-conflict card, done, and #4 offers Merge again. Two polls later no card was open (20).

J6 (bench/rebase), W15-06:
- I pressed Redo on the Tasks row with no card open, pushed a conflicting page.html to main and ran a session.
- One card: title '"Write the page in page.html" conflicts with main', body "Its branch conflicts with main in page.html, and the agent could not resolve it.", three one-line explanations, and a last step "... and updates #2" (24-j6-inbox-rebase-card.png).

Not walked on the bench:
- W15-03 (a busy middle cannot be staged by hand) and W15-07 (the bench has no switch for lazy mergeability). Both are covered by their composed tests, which fail on the base.

The bench is stopped with stop.mjs; its home, fake GitHub repos and browser profile are deleted.

- With the base's source and the new tests (git checkout 931ed52 of the 16 changed source files, restored afterwards), 20 of the 22 new 'w15-merge' runtime and capabilities cases fail.
- The W15-07 case fails with the lazy stand-in and the base watcher.
- Both new real-daemon cases (W15-01, W15-05) fail on the base.
- On the fix branch everything below is green: pnpm lint, typecheck, pnpm test (481 files, 4998 passed), test:e2e (25 passed), test:integration (30 passed), the UI vitest suite (1025), Playwright with the local config (35), docs-check --base 931ed52, link-check and secret-scan.

blocking.issue: W15-02 with W15-05: a commit the person pushes to GitHub, as the new sentence tells them to, is taken as reviewed by the rebuild. The row then offers Merge under 'Reviewed by the critic', and a Merge pressed during the commit wait (now kept by the merge route) makes Forerunner merge the unreviewed commit by itself. The guide's own promise ('#8 waits for your look, since the review did not read it') and ADR 0111 ('a commit pushed to the branch afterwards is never merged by Forerunner') are both broken.
blocking.evidence: Bench J3 (bench/chain2): commit in B's folder, A squash-merged, row says '#3 waits for a commit made in its task's folder: push it to GitHub or undo it.', push from the folder. The next poll set merge_record reviewed_head_sha=8ef38a9 (top commit 'My own change'), last_outcome not_allowed, and the Overview offers Merge (/tmp/frbench/review-w15-merge/steps/10-j3-overview-after-push.png). Bench J4 (bench/chain3): the same, with POST /projects/:id/pull-requests/3/merge pressed during the wait (answer queued). After the push, #3 was merged by Forerunner and mine.txt is on main (steps/j4-checks.json). A composed test appended for the run only reproduces it: after.reviewed_head_sha equals the PR head holding notes.txt. Root cause: settleRecord compares r.ownBefore with r.ownAfter, both read from GitHub's branch, which already holds the pushed commit. It never compares against record.own_change_id or reviewed_head_sha. The fixer's test 'pushed to GitHub, as the sentence offers' only passes because A is closed there (rebuilt_without), not squash-merged.
blocking.expected: A rebuild whose GitHub branch is not the reviewed head (r.before differs from record.reviewed_head_sha), or whose own change before the rebuild differs from record.own_change_id, leaves the record to the person ('changed after the review' or 'look before you merge'). It never moves reviewed_head_sha onto that head, and it drops a kept person approval. Test: the W15-02 'pushed' case with A squash-merged, plus a variant with Merge pressed during the commit wait. #N must stay unmerged and offer no plain Merge.

blocking.issue: W15-01: the second project's status 'stays in the app', but the app never shows it. B's Docs tab says docs/status.md is 'not written yet' after B's session wrote it. The user guide written in this fix ('keeps its own status under Docs in the app') and ADR 0106's amendment ('its status stays in the app (as with the setting off)') promise what the code does not do.
blocking.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:442-446 (statusDocRoot returns null whenever the status pull request is on); docs.ts:905; docs/user-guide.md:321
blocking.evidence: Bench J1: after B's session, home/data/projects/<B>/app-status/docs/status.md exists and the log has 'status pull request not written: another project's status pull request is open'. B's Docs tab shows 'Status docs/status.md missing / not written yet' (/tmp/frbench/review-w15-merge/steps/03-j1-b-docs-tab.png). GET /projects/<B>/docs/docs%2Fstatus.md answers 404 'docs/status.md is not written yet' (steps/j1b-checks.json, review-state.json docsBStatus).
blocking.expected: While another project's status PR blocks this one, the Docs tab (and the chat's docs search) reads the status the session kept in the app, as it does with the setting off. That copy stops being preferred once this project's own status PR is written again. Add a real-daemon or loop-docs assertion on GET /projects/:id/docs for B.

blocking.issue: W15-04: the Tasks-row Redo now withdraws the task's open merge card and marks it redo_from_base. The move's change does not record that, so Undo of the Redo puts the task back to done but leaves the conflict card withdrawn for good, with an unused redo_from_base mark. The Redo's own line does not say the card closed. No undo test was added, though the spec asks that every undo be tested.
blocking.where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:1004-1021 (taskReopen: the cards are withdrawn outside personMove, so after.withdrawn_requests and the sentence miss them; undoMove reopens only after.withdrawn_requests)
blocking.evidence: A composed test appended to dependent-branches-merge.test.ts for the run only, then restored: conflicting pair, poll (1 notice), taskReopen.run (source ui). The sentence was 'Reopened "Write the other page" to redo it: the next session works on it again.' and after was {task_id,status:ready,title}. I then ran taskReopen.undo and polled twice: task done, record last_outcome 'conflict', 0 open cards. The card stays withdrawn with outcome 'redone' and redo_from_base:true. The conflict notice is 'said once', so it never comes back (expected 1 open card, got 0).
blocking.expected: Record the withdrawn merge cards in after.withdrawn_requests, so Undo reopens them, and strip their redo mark. Make the Redo's line say the card closed and the task is done again from main (design §3.8). Add an undo test across a restart (validation rule 4).

non_blocking: W15-07: the re-read is capped per PR (githost-watcher.ts:567, up to 15 s for each PR, read one after another), not per poll as the decision ('about 15 s in all') and the acceptance ('at most about 15 s per poll') say. After a main move, N null PRs can hold one poll for N×15 s. It also uses a real setTimeout that stop() does not cancel.
